transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The architect of Tennessee's Lethal Injection Protocols is stepping down from his position.
From member station WPLN in Nashville, Mariana Baca-Yau reports, this comes after a second
botched execution this year.
Frank Strada helped design the state's new execution process after a 2020 review found
that Tennessee had not properly inspected the drugs it uses to put people to death.
Strada came to Tennessee from Arizona, where he oversaw three botched executions similar
to Wednesday's.
Christa Pike did not die after receiving two full doses of pentobarbital.
Usually just one dose is considered lethal.
Pike's attorneys say she is unconscious and on a ventilator at an area hospital following
Wednesday's botched execution.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Baca-Yau in Nashville.
President Trump is taking his midterm campaign swing into more competitive territory.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports Trump will visit Ohio after stops in Republican-dominated states.
The president is traveling to Vandalia, Ohio, to support Republican Senator John Husted,
who is facing a tight race against Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown.
Brown is seeking a comeback after losing his Senate seat, while Husted is a relatively
new incumbent.
He has served in the Senate for just two years after being appointed to fill the seat vacated
by J.D. Vance when Vance became vice president.
Ohio could offer an early test of how Republicans in swing states navigate Trump heading into
these midterms.
They can either embrace the president and use his ability to energize the Republican base,
or create some distance from him to appeal to more moderate voters.
Franco, Ordonez, NPR News, The White House.
Five Palestinians were killed in an Israeli airstrike on a home in Gaza City early today.
And Pearson-Hasbaba reports it's the latest Israeli attack despite what's supposed to
be nearly one year of a cease-fire in Gaza.
Inside St. Porphyrios Church, mourners gather around the bodies of 56-year-old Mesa and
her 35-year-old daughter Maria.
The women were part of a small community of Palestinian Christians who had survived Israel's
attack on Gaza for the past three years.
They were killed just after midnight by an Israeli missile strike on their building.
Gaza's Health Ministry says three others were also killed, a female university professor,
her mother, and a young man.
Christians leader in Gaza estimate only about 400 Christians remain in the territory, down
from around 1,000 before the war.
The Israeli military did not immediately respond to NPR's request for a comment on the attack.
An Asbaba NPR News, Gaza City.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Major League Baseball's divisional round of playoffs gets underway today with games
in four cities.
In Milwaukee, the Brewers face the San Diego Padres in a matchup that raises questions
about how much a team's payroll determines its ability to compete.
This is a labor dispute bruise, with Major League's pitching a salary cap.
Chuck Hornbach has more.
The Brewers have the best record in baseball during the regular season despite having the
smallest market size and a payroll in the bottom half of Major League clubs.
The Padres payroll is in the top third, but Milwaukee fan John Matta says his team can
win the best of five series because it has more heart and manager Pat Murphy.
He does something right with those guys.
I mean, he's got the right attitude.
He leads them well.
He does good things with them.
A possible salary cap and the competitive balance between teams are expected to be controversial
issues during a potential labor dispute after this month's World Series.
For NPR News, I'm Chuck Hornbach in Milwaukee.
The Supreme Court opens its new term Monday and will hear cases on religion, bans on semi-automatic
weapons, climate change, immigration, and election law.
The opening case Monday will center on climate change and whether state and local governments
can sue energy companies for allegedly deceiving the public about the damaging effects of fossil
fuels.
One of the biggest cases so far is on religion over whether taxpayers should fund religious
schools that refuse to admit LGBTQ students and parents.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Tennessee lethal injection architect Frank Strada steps down after second botched execution this year
President Trump campaigns in Ohio supporting Republican Senator John Husted against Democrat Sherrod Brown
Five Palestinians killed in Israeli airstrike on Gaza City home amid ongoing cease-fire
Major League Baseball divisional playoffs begin with Brewers facing Padres despite payroll disparities
Supreme Court begins new term hearing cases on religion, weapons bans, climate, immigration, elections
